items.heading: Sacred groves
details: Religious protection of certain forest patches has long helped preserve biodiversity and natural vegetation.

items.heading: Sacred-tree traditions
details: Cultural restrictions around specific trees have helped protect many mature, long-lived trees.

items.heading: Snake-worship traditions
details: Cultural reverence for snakes can discourage killing them, supporting a natural pest-control species.

items.heading: Traditional protection of ponds and water bodies
details: Community restrictions around water bodies can help preserve them for everyone's long-term use.

items.heading: Sacred plant cultivation
details: Encourages the ongoing preservation and propagation of culturally important plant species.

items.heading: Worshipping nature (rivers, trees, animals)
details: Treating rivers like the Ganga, mountains, cows, and trees as sacred encouraged communities to protect and conserve them.
This reverence functioned as an early, community-enforced form of ecological conservation.

items.heading: Traditional community grazing management
details: Regulated, shared grazing practices can prevent excessive pressure on common pastureland.
